title: Seller evidence kits: SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a field-ready evidence & messaging kit for sellers and solutions engineers to use in pre-RFP, discovery, and security reviews. Focus: practical answers to SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness, data handling expectations (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and standardized audit-log language.

TL;DR (one-liners for quick comms):
- Redwood is production-first: we combine a hardened inference runtime with auditable controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.
- SOC2: We maintain SOC2 Type II readiness for our hosted control plane and offer control mapping and evidence bundles for Dedicated/Private customers.
- HIPAA: Redwood can be configured for HIPAA-safe deployments (BAA for Dedicated/Private; data-plane separation + customer KMS).
- Audit logs: We provide immutable request/response metadata, token-level cost records, and configurable retention to satisfy most enterprise audits.

Suggested opening paragraph for sales emails / proposals:
Redwood Inference is built to make LLM inference predictable, auditable, and secure at scale. For regulated workloads we offer Flexible Deployment (Hosted API with SOC2-aligned control plane, Reserved Dedicated capacity with contractual isolation, and Private/VPC installs for full data control). Below are concise talking points and the evidence matrix your buyer will ask for.

Field kit: what to attach to an initial security review
- One-page architecture diagram per deployment option (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Control-mapping spreadsheet (SOC2 / ISO 27001 high-level mapping to Redwood features and artifacts).
- Sample audit-log extract (anonymized) + description of fields.
- HIPAA readiness checklist + sample BAA summary (for legal).
- Pen-test summary and dates (red team results + remediation summary).
- Contact card for security review: security@redwood.ai and named SE.

SOC2 readiness — field notes and seller language:
- Scope: Our hosted control plane and ops teams are covered by SOC2-aligned policies; customers running Dedicated or Private may ask for a control mapping that shows which controls remain vendor responsibility vs customer responsibility (we call this the Shared Responsibility Matrix).
- Evidence commonly requested: policy docs (access control, change mgmt), SIEM/alerting screenshots, incident response runbook summary, user access lists, background-check policy for personnel with access.
- Seller script: “We can provide a control mapping and an evidence bundle within 3–5 business days for Hosted customers. For Dedicated and Private, we provide tailored artifacts and a short engagement to define in-scope controls.”

SOC2 control mapping (quick primer for SEs):
- Logical access: RBAC and SSO + central identity provider (SCIM/Okta) integration.
- System config/change: Git-backed infra-as-code, PR history for runtime builds, and signed release artifacts.
- Availability/monitoring: Per-route latency SLAs, per-route health metrics in Console, and SRE runbooks.
- Logging and retention: Audit logs with write-once storage for customer request metadata; retention configurable per contract.
- Encryption: KMS integration for keys at rest and TLS for transit.

HIPAA readiness — practical details for buyers
- Modes: Hosted can be covered under a BAA for certain usage patterns where Redwood processes PHI on behalf of customer. For the highest assurance, recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where customer data resides in isolated capacity or VPC and keys are customer-managed.
- Data flow guidance: Always treat prompt + user identifiers as PHI if they include health info. Recommend non-identifiable embeddings unless explicitly needed. Use prefix stripping / redaction before logs are retained.
- Key contractual asks we can support: BAA, data deletion commitments, control mapping for PHI handling, encryption key custody (customer KMS), and audit log exports for ePHI access.

Audit-log language — boilerplate for proposals (pick & edit):
- “Redwood provides request-level audit logs containing timestamp, authenticated principal, model/version, route, input size (token counts), and response metadata. For Dedicated/Private deployments logs can be exported to customer-owned storage and retention policies adjusted per contract. Logs are append-only and protected via RBAC and immutability controls.”
- Optional: “We support near-real-time log streaming to customer SIEM (via secure forwarding) and S3-compatible export for long-term archival.”

Competitive posture (notes vs. common competitors):
- Comp A (large API provider): Strength: brand trust and wide array of managed models. Weakness: limited private deployment options and less field-level audit customization. Redwood angle: emphasize private installs and audit-log exports + production runtime telemetry.
- Comp B (self-hosted runtime vendor): Strength: deep runtime optimizations, full customer control. Weakness: heavy ops burden and no unified managed control plane. Redwood angle: unified control plane + optional private install — we remove ops burden while preserving control.
- Comp C (platform-focused AI vendor): Strength: SLAs and marketplace footprint. Weakness: opaque model performance and coarse-grained cost telemetry. Redwood angle: token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and rollout controls to reduce quality regressions.

Common buyer objections and quick rebuttals:
- “We need a BAA.” → Rebuttal: “We can execute a BAA for Dedicated and Private customers; for Hosted customer use-cases we’ll run a short intake to determine eligibility and provide a BAA when appropriate.”
- “How can I prove logs weren’t altered?” → Rebuttal: “Logs are written to an append-only store with cryptographic checksums for Dedicated/Private. We provide export & streaming to customer storage for independent verification.”
- “Who has access to customer data?” → Rebuttal: “Access is strictly limited via RBAC; we provide a list of staff roles with potential access and background-check policies as part of the evidence bundle.”

Sales play: tailored evidence bundles by buyer profile
- Small SaaS buyer (low-risk): send 1-pager + sample logs + SOC2 mapping.
- Regulated enterprise (PHI/PII heavy): propose Dedicated or Private, include BAA draft, key custody options, and a joint scoping call with Security/Infra.
- Platform/integrator partners: include SIEM connectors, long-retention options, and third-party audit summary.

Quick checklist for SE before security call:
- ✅ Pick deployment recommendation (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) based on PII/PHI need.
- ✅ Attach SOC2 control mapping PDF and sample audit log extract.
- ✅ Confirm whether customer requires KMS/HSM and if so whether they have preferred vendor.
- ✅ Prepare redaction/retention proposal for any PHI in prompts.
- ✅ Schedule 30-min deep dive with Security if legal/security owner is involved.

Open questions we still need to finalize (owner in parentheses):
- Standard retention buckets and pricing for log retention beyond 7 years (Finance/Product) — owner: Ethan Nguyen.
- Definitive Hosted-BAA eligibility rubric and intake form (Legal/Security) — owner: Lena Morales.
- Sample anonymized audit-log extract with checksum metadata for customer demo (Security/IR) — owner: Samir Kaur.

Next steps (this doc is a living kit):
1) Validate the control-mapping spreadsheet with Security (due in 2 weeks).
2) Produce a one-page HIPAA BAA summary and attach to the legal bundle.
3) Create two canned email templates (intro + evidence delivery) for the Sales CRM.

Notes to field: keep artifacts short and pragmatic. Buyers want: clear answers, a map of who owns which control, and the ability to validate logs in their own environment. Use the TL;DR bullets at the top of this doc in the first outreach.
